out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: Open drinking containers used or stored in a manner that may contaminate food, food contact surfaces or utensils. Observed open cups stored on prep surfaces of cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may have beverages in the kitchen areas as long as they are covered and consumed through a straw and stored in a manner that will prevent contamination to food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items. Personal in charge discarded beverages.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: chicken soup (84F) in soup warmer; cooked lamb (64F) in 2 drawer warmer.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. Person in charge reheated soup to 204F and reheated lamb to 165F.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours: cooked rice (73F) after 2 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. Person in charge discarded rice.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: spinach pie (118F), cooked gyro (109F), cooked pork (100F) on cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. Person in charge reheated all items to 165F or above.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: handles of cold holding equipment on cook line.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Person in charge cleaned all equipment.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of dust; walk-in refrigerator fans have a build-up of dust which may come into contact with foods in the cooling rack area.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

violations.title: Backflow Prevention, Approved Device Provided
violations.observation: Observed the lack of an approved backflow prevention device on the water supply system. Mop sink is connected directly to a chemical dispensing unit and the water is kept turned on.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be installed to preclude backflow of a solid, liquid, or gas contaminant into the water supply system at each point of use at the food establishment, including on a hose bib if a hose is attached or on a hose bib if a hose is not attached and backflow prevention is required by Law by installing an approved backflow prevention device as specified under 5-202.14. EHS discussed with PIC the importance of the Backflow AVB device installed at the mop sink. Hose connections should be removed when not in use and water should be kept off to prevent a buildup of pressure at the mop sink which may result in failure of the backflow AVB.
